purpose: Baseline distribution of gate-bypass reason codes used to seed ADR 0453 thresholds. Establishes the 30d-prior state at the moment ADR 0453 enters Proposed status.

pre_existing_gate_failures.notes: Concentrated around ws-0346, ws-0364–ws-0374, ws-0417 main-merge sequence (April 12–14). The repeat pattern is the strongest evidence that gate erosion is real and ADR 0453's gate_bypass_repeat_reasons_30d metric would have surfaced it earlier.

gate_timeout.notes: All three are ws-0374 merge-main retries on the same day. Likely the same root-cause incident split across pushes.

reclassification_notes: All 19 bypasses in the window already use valid reason codes from config/gate-bypass-waiver-catalog.json per ADR 0267. The earlier metrics review counted 4 'bypasses' from git-grep — those were governance commits *recording* bypasses, not the bypasses themselves. No retroactive reclassification needed.

threshold_recommendation.rationale: Baseline of 19 is dominated by a two-day cluster of legitimate pre-existing failures during the ws-0346/ws-0374/main-merge sequence. A threshold of 8/30d is achievable in a normal month and would flag clustered remediation pushes the way they should be flagged. Repeat threshold of 3 catches systemic gate erosion without firing on isolated retries.

follow_ups.action: Generator script consumes this baseline file as the seed for build/integration-health.json on first run.

Audit whether the certificate-mismatch lane that drove most of these bypasses was permanently fixed by ADR 0414/0415, or whether residual cases remain. If permanent, the baseline should drop substantially in the next audit.
